Short links for password-less shares — opt-in, via a server master key.

By default a password-less share carries its decryption key in the URL
`#fragment`, which keeps the link end-to-end (the server can never decrypt it)
but makes it long. Set a `MASTER_KEY` and password-less uploads switch to a new
**server mode**: the per-file key is wrapped with the master key and stored, so
the link is just `…/d/aB3xK` — no fragment. Password shares are untouched and
stay end-to-end.

## Added

- **Server encryption mode → short links.** A new third at-rest mode alongside
  *password* and *link*. When `MASTER_KEY` is set, a password-less upload wraps
  its per-file age key with the master key and stores it, instead of returning
  the key in the share URL. The recipient just opens the short link — the server
  decrypts with its master key, no credential needed.
- **`MASTER_KEY` config.** New optional environment variable (Unraid template
  field, masked). Generate one with `openssl rand -base64 32`. It lives only in
  the container environment, never in the `/data` volume — a stolen data backup
  stays unreadable. Keep it secret and **back it up**: losing it makes
  password-less files unrecoverable. Empty = the existing long `#key` links.
- **Template dropdowns.** `ENCRYPT_UPLOADS` (`true | false`) and
  `DEFAULT_EXPIRY` (`7d | 1h | 6h | 1d | 30d | never`) are now pick-lists in the
  Unraid template instead of free-text fields.

## How the modes compare

| Share type | Key wrapped with | Link | Server can decrypt? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Password** | your password | `…/d/<slug>` | No — not even the operator |
| **Server** (`MASTER_KEY` set, no password) | the server master key | `…/d/<slug>` — **short** | Yes (holds the master key); a stolen *data* backup alone cannot |
| **Link** (no master key, no password) | — (key in `#fragment`) | `…/d/<slug>#k=…` — long | No — the key never reaches the server |

## Compatibility

Fully backward-compatible. With `MASTER_KEY` unset, behaviour is identical to
v2.1.x: password-less shares keep their long `#fragment` links. The mode is
recorded per file, so files already stored keep the mode they were created with.
